sentences.text: In connection with the accident, FIR no.248/2018, under section 279/304-A IPC was registered at PS Madhu Vihar on the statement of an eye-witness namely Ankit, who explained the whole incident and prayed for legal action against the respondent no.1 who caused the accident by driving the offending bus rashly and negligently.
After completion of the investigation, charge-sheet was filed before the concerned court and the instant DAR was filed before this Tribunal for the grant of compensation to the claimants.
3. All the respondents appeared and filed their replies to the DAR/ claim petition.

__ 4. Respondent no.1 and 2 in their joint written statement stated that the accident was caused due to negligence of the deceased himself, who was driving the motorcycle in zig-zag manner and suddenly his motorcycle got slipped and came under the back wheel of the offending bus resulting into death of the deceased.

Rest, the insurance company took general defences.

My findings on the issues are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1

Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle no.UP15CT-4083 on 02.08.2018 at about 09:30 p.m., near Rain Basera, Anand Vihar B u s A d d a , D e l h i , i n r a s h a n d n e g l i g e n t m a n n e r ______________________________________________________________________ and caused the death of deceased Nadim Kureshi? OPP 11.
It is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 &
Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

UP15CT-4083 hit a motorcycle bearing no. DL5SBB-1116 from the back side, due to which motorcycle became unbalanced and motorcyclist along with motorcycle fell under the left rear tyre of the said bus which run over the motorcyclist along with motorcycle.

The eye-witness PW1 has given further detailed description of the manner of accident in his cross-examination also, wherein he stated that he was coming from Noida and going to his residence via Anand Vihar and when he reached at EDM Mall, near Rainbasera, Anand Vihar, Delhi, he saw that the bus bearing no. UP16CT 4083 hit the back rear portion of the motorcycle bearing no.1116 (motorcycle of deceased).
PW1 stated that the road was wide enough to accommodate two-three vehicles at a time and he was driving just behind the motorcycle (of deceased) about 25 metres back.
PW1 stated that the offending bus was in the middle of the road.
He stated that the street lights were on and the road was illuminated.
The bus was going straight and there was no left turn near the place of accident.
The motorcyclist was wearing a helmet.
PW1 stated that the offending bus after causing the accident was stopped by the public at a distance of about 20-25 yards from the place of the accident.

14. It is evident that during the entire testimony of eye-witness PW1, nothing came on record which may demolish or discredit his testimony on the aspect of a rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 while driving the offending vehicle.
Besides, nothing else is available on record which may suggest any falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of the eye-witness.

sentences.text: Thus, it may be discernible that respondent no.1 was negligent in driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.

19. Not only this, the respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted in the criminal case by the police after detailed investigation and in a motor vehicle accident claim case, which support the version of petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
20.
Further, there is no challenge from the respondent no. 1/ driver of the offending vehicle to the version of the petitioners.

The respondent no.1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the testimony of the eye-witness (PW1) regarding the above accident and its manner but he preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.

Thus,
an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009(3) AD (Delhi) 310.

22. The MLC no. 010690 dated 02/08/2018 of the respondent no.1/driver of the offending vehicle shows that the respondent no.1 was under the influence of alcohol whose Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) was 100.
Driving a bus under the influence of alcohol is per se rash and negligent act.

23. Thus, in the light of the above discussion and the evidence brought on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of the preponderance of probabilities that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into fatal injuries to deceased Nadim Kureshi.
Issue no.1 is, accordingly, decided in favour of petitioners.

sentences.text: Decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should b e ______________________________________________________________________ determined.
Out of the said income, a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.

sentences.text: Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family (multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:
______________________________________________________________________ PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased 26.

The copy of Aadhaar Card of deceased Nadim Kureshi at page no.6 of the DAR reflects his date of birth as 02.04.1994, which would mean that on the date of accident (02.08.2018), the age of deceased was 24 years.
Assessment of Income of deceased 27.
No evidence has been led with respect to the income, occupation and education of the deceased.

As per Aadhaar Card of the deceased, he was residing at Loni Dehat,
Ghaziabad, U.P.
Therefore, income of deceased be assessed at par with minimum wages applicable to an unskilled category worker of Uttar Pradesh on the date of accident (02.08.2018), which were Rs.7,613- per month.
Thus, the income of the deceased is considered to be Rs.7,613/- per month.
Application of Multiplier Dar - Smt. Nano vs Sunder Singh on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175279071/
As determined above, the age of the deceased was 24 years on the date of the accident.

Hence, multiplier of 18 shall be applicable in case of the deceased herein,
who belonged to age group between 21- 25 year (refer: Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121).
Future Prospects 29.

The deceased can be considered a self-employed and therefore, an addition of 40% to the income of the deceased, who was below 40 years of age, has to be considered towards future prospects [(refer:
Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra)].
______________________________________________________________________ Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses 30.
As per DAR, the deceased left behind his parents and seven siblings.
Further, no evidence has come on record that the deceased was a married person.

Hence,
considering the marital status of the deceased as unmarried, 50% of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards his personal living expenses (refer: Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65).

sentences.text: Loss of Dependency 31.

In view of the settled guidelines as laid down in the various judgments herein above, by adding the future prospects @ 40% to the annual income of the deceased, applying the multiplier of 18 and making one-third deduction towards personal living expenses of the deceased, the loss of dependency is computed as Rs.11,51,086/- (7,613x140/100x1/2 x18x12).
NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES 32.

In the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, dated 31.10.2017, in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. (AIR 2017 SC 5157), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium,
loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 &
Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
12.
Thus, it may be discernible that respondent no.1 was negligent in driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.
The respondent no.1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the testimony of the eye-witness (PW1) regarding the above accident and its manner but he preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.
Thus,
an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009(3) AD (Delhi) 310.
21.
Driving a bus under the influence of alcohol is per se rash and negligent act.
Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death:
(a) age of the deceased;
(b) income of the deceased; and (c) the number of dependents.
These issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are:
(i) additions/deductions to be made for arriving at the income;
(ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased;
and iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should b e ______________________________________________________________________ determined.
Out of the said income, a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
The annual contribution to the family (multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Assessment of Income of deceased 27.
No evidence has been led with respect to the income, occupation and education of the deceased.
As per Aadhaar Card of the deceased, he was residing at Loni Dehat,
Ghaziabad, U.P.
Therefore, income of deceased be assessed at par with minimum wages applicable to an unskilled category worker of Uttar Pradesh on the date of accident (02.08.2018), which were Rs.7,613- per month.
Thus, the income of the deceased is considered to be Rs.7,613/- per month.
Hence, multiplier of 18 shall be applicable in case of the deceased herein,
who belonged to age group between 21- 25 year (refer: Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121).
opennyai_summary.decision:
Issue no.1 is, accordingly, decided in favour of petitioners.
In view of the settled guidelines as laid down in the various judgments herein above, by adding the future prospects @ 40% to the annual income of the deceased, applying the multiplier of 18 and making one-third deduction towards personal living expenses of the deceased, the loss of dependency is computed as Rs.11,51,086/- (7,613x140/100x1/2 x18x12).
NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES 32.
In the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, dated 31.10.2017, in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. (AIR 2017 SC 5157), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium,
loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
33.
